Ji'an|China.f: Ji'an is short for its original name Jitai Min'an, and the city was formerly known as Luling and Jizhou.

Bengbu|China.f: Bengbu means Clam Wharf in Chinese, a nod to its past as a freshwater pearl fishery that earned it the nickname Pearl City.

Qinhuangdao|China.f: Its name means Qin Emperor island, from the legend that the First Emperor of Qin held a ritual here in 210 BC on his last tour.

Handan|China.f: Handan was capital of the state of Zhao for 158 years, and scholars credit it as the source of more than 1,500 Chinese idioms.

Linfen|China.f: Linfen's Yaodu District is named for the legendary ruler Yao, whose capital Chinese archaeologists have placed here.

L\u00fcliang|China.f: This Shanxi city faces Shaanxi across the Yellow River, and reproductive biologist Min Chueh Chang was born here in 1908.

Shuozhou|China.f: Shuozhou's Yingxian Tower, built in 1056 under the Liao dynasty, is made entirely of wood without using nails.

Wuhai|China.f: Wuhai's antipode lies almost exactly on the city of Valdivia, Chile, a rare case of two inhabited cities opposite each other.

Bayannur|China.f: Bayannur means Rich Lake in Mongolian, and the area was a league until it became a prefecture-level city on 1 December 2003.

Chenzhou|China.f: Tang poets such as Du Fu and Han Yu visited Chenzhou, which today is a production base for tungsten, bismuth and molybdenum.

Yongzhou|China.f: Yongzhou is the southernmost prefecture-level division in Hunan and is home to 49 ethnic groups, 48 of them minorities.

Shaoyang|China.f: Shaoyang was called Baoqing until 1928, when it became Shaoyang County, and its history stretches back about 2,500 years.

Yulin (Guangxi)|China.f: Yulin's name was changed in 1956 from characters meaning Dense Forest to Jade Forest, which sound identical in Mandarin.

Yueyang|China.f: Yueyang Tower is counted with the Pavilion of Prince Teng and Yellow Crane Tower as one of the Three Great Towers of Jiangnan.

Jingzhou|China.f: The Chinese proverb carelessness lost Jingzhou dates to the Three Kingdoms, when general Guan Yu lost the city to Eastern Wu.

Shiyan|China.f: Shiyan grew from a village of a few hundred households in the 1960s into a Dongfeng truck city with China's second-highest living standard.

Xiangyang|China.f: Xiangyang and Fancheng held out against the Mongols for six years before surrendering in the Siege of Xiangyang.

Qingyang|China.f: A reported meteor shower in 1490 rained stones on Qingyang and is said to have killed more than 10,000 people.

Cangyuan|China.f: Ochre cliff paintings at 15 sites in Cangyuan show more than 1,200 figures and are dated to the late Neolithic.

Lancang|China.f: The ancient tea forests around Jingmai Mountain in Lancang County are inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

Heze|China.f: Heze calls itself the Peony Capital of China, and over 30% of its GDP reportedly comes from selling peonies.

Rizhao|China.f: Rizhao has required solar water heaters in buildings since the early 1990s, and by 2007 99% of central households used them.

Sanming|China.f: Sha County in Sanming has 39 snacks labeled Famous Chinese Snacks and 63 labeled Famous Fujian Snacks.

Weifang|China.f: Weifang hosted the first international kite festival in 1984, with participants from eleven countries.

Weihai|China.f: Weihai is the mainland Chinese city closest to South Korea, and Britain ruled its core under lease from 1898 to 1930.

Bijie|China.f: Bijie was the only prefecture-level city in Guizhou with no rail service until the Leshan-Guiyang Railway opened in 2020.

Dazhou|China.f: Red Army leaders Xu Xiangqian, Li Xiannian and Xu Shiyou were all from or lived in Dazhou.

Kaili|China.f: Kaili is the center of Miao culture and hosts more than 120 festivals a year, earning the name Town of a Hundred Festivals.

Renhuai|China.f: Maotai spirit, made in Renhuai, won a medal at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, which spurred demand within China.

Yibin|China.f: Yibin is where the Jinsha River becomes the Yangtze, known in Chinese as Chang Jiang, the Long River.

Bole|China.f: Sayram Lake near Bole sits at 2,073 m, the highest and largest lake in Xinjiang, nicknamed the last teardrop of the Atlantic.

Fuyun|China.f: Fuyun County has recorded a low of -51.5 C, and about 74% of its residents are Kazakhs.

Anshan|China.f: Anshan holds a jade Buddha carved from a single 260.76-ton stone, and about a third of the world's talc supply.

Baishan|China.f: Baishan means White Mountain, after Changbai Mountain, and the city took that name only in April 1994.

Dandong|China.f: Dandong was renamed in 1965 from Andong, meaning pacifying the east, to Dandong, meaning red east.

Mudanjiang|China.f: Imperial Russia built a Chinese Eastern Railway station at Mudanjiang in 1903, which kicked off the town's growth.

Yanji|China.f: In 2010 over a thousand Yanbian University students juggled soccer balls at once to set a Guinness world record.

Changde|China.f: Changde's Poetry Wall runs 3 km along the Yuan River and is listed by Guinness as the longest wall with engraved arts.

Zhangjiakou|China.f: The Beijing-Zhangjiakou Railway, finished in 1909, was the first railway designed and built solely by Chinese people.

Zhalantun|China.f: Zhalantun was formerly known as Butha, was renamed Yalu county in 1929, and became Zalantun Banner in 1933.
